provenance.title: Exact Results for Perturbative Chern-Simons Theory with Complex Gauge Group
provenance.authors: Tudor Dimofte,1 Sergei Gukov,1,2 Jonatan Lenells,3 and Don Zagier4,5

candidates.statement: However, in some cases (which include Chern-Simons gauge theory), the coupling constant must obey certain quantization conditions, which, therefore, can lead to a "preferred" normalization of $\hbar$ up to irrelevant $\mathbb{Q}$-valued factors.

This should be contrasted with the case of a compact gauge group, where one usually develops perturbation theory in the background of a trivial flat connection, and the perturbative invariants $S_n^{(\rho)}$ turn out to be rational numbers.
As we shall see below, in many cases the representation $\rho$ admits continuous deformations or, put differently, comes in a family.

As we shall see, the perturbative $G_{{\mathbb{C}}}$ invariant $Z^{(\rho)} (M;\hbar)$ is a function of the deformation parameters, which on the *geometric branch*[^1] can be interpreted as shape parameters of the associated hyperbolic structure.
As we shall see below, this normalization is especially natural from the viewpoint of the analytic continuation approach.

Since we are interested only in the "holomorphic" sector of the theory, we shall look only at the kinetic term for the field ${\cal A}$ (and not $\bar {\cal A}$); it leads to a holomorphic symplectic 2-form on ${{\cal M}}_{{\rm flat}}(G_{{\mathbb{C}}}, \Sigma)$: $$\omega \;=\; {i \over 4 \hbar} \int_{\Sigma} {\rm Tr}~ \delta {\cal A}\wedge \delta {\cal A}\,. \label{msympl}$$ We note that this symplectic structure does not depend on the complex structure of $\Sigma$, in accord with the topological nature of the theory.

The moduli space of flat $G_{{\mathbb{C}}}$ connections on a 3-manifold $M$ with a single toral boundary, $\partial M = T^2$, defines a complex Lagrangian submanifold $${\cal L}\subset ( {\Bbb{T}}_{{\mathbb{C}}} \times {\Bbb{T}}_{{\mathbb{C}}} ) / {\cal W}\;.$$ (More precisely, this Lagrangian submanifold comprises the top-dimensional (stable) components of the moduli space of flat $G_{{\mathbb{C}}}$ connections on $\Sigma$.) In particular, a generic irreducible component of ${\cal L}$ is defined by $r$ polynomial equations $$A_i (l,m) \;=\; 0\,, \qquad i = 1, \ldots, r\,, \label{aizero}$$ which must be invariant under the action of the Weyl group ${\cal W}$ (which simultaneously acts on the eigenvalues $l_1, \ldots, l_r$ and $m_1, \ldots, m_r$).

Indeed, as we shall describe in Section [\[sec:analytic\]](#sec:analytic){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:analytic"}, this relation may be used to justify the "analytic continuation" approach to computing perturbative $G_{{\mathbb{C}}}$ invariants.
It should nevertheless be noted that the analytic continuation described here is not as "analytic" as it sounds.
Therefore, since our main goal is to solve the *quantum* theory (to all orders in perturbation theory) we shall not worry about this ambiguity in the classical term.

Assuming that the $\sim \pm\frac{i}{2} {\mbox{Vol\,}}(M;u)$ behavior of the geometric and conjugate branches is unique, their signed and conjugate pairs must coincide for amphicheiral 3-manifolds. $S_0^{(\rm geom)}$, then, is an even analytic function of $u$ with strictly real series coefficients; at $u \in i {\mathbb{R}}$, the Chern-Simons invariant ${\rm CS} (M;u)$ will vanish.
One must remember, however, that vertices of tetrahedra are not part of $M$, and that the combined boundaries of their neighborhoods in $M$ are not spheres, but tori.
First, the product of the shape parameters $z_j^{(i)}$ at every edge in the triangulation must be equal to 1, in order for the hyperbolic structures of adjacent tetrahedra to match.

More precisely, the sum of some chosen branches of $\log z_j^{(i)}$ (equal to the standard branch if one is near the complete structure) should equal $2\pi i$, so that the total dihedral angle at each edge is $2\pi$.

To proceed, one must first make sure that the three shape parameters $z^{(i)}=z_1^{(i)}$, $z_2^{(i)}$, and $z_3^{(i)}$ are specifically assigned to edges $[v_1^{(i)},v_2^{(i)}]$, $[v_1^{(i)},v_3^{(i)}]$, and $[v_1^{(i)},v_2^{(i)}]$ (respectively) in each tetrahedron $\Delta_i$ of an oriented triangulation of $M$, where $[v_a^{(i)},v_b^{(i)}]$ denotes the edge going from numbered vertex $v_a^{(i)}$ to numbered vertex $v_b^{(i)}$.

For a consistent labeling of the triangulation, called a "combinatorial flattening," the sum of log-parameters $w^{(i)}_j$ around every edge must vanish, and the (signed[^3]) sum of log-parameters along the two paths generating $\pi_1(T^2)={\mathbb{Z}}^2$ for any boundary (cusp) $T^2$ must equal twice the logarithm of the $SL(2,{\mathbb{C}})$ holonomies around these paths.

[^4]: []{#foot:v2pi label="foot:v2pi"}Explicitly, in the notation of Section [\[sec:quantization\]](#sec:quantization){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:quantization"} and above, the sum of log-parameters along the two paths in the neighborhood of the $k$th cusp must equal $2u_k$ and $2v_k+2\pi i$, respectively.

(Physicists should think of these spaces as "Hilbert" spaces obtained by quantizing the theory on a manifold with boundary.) The elements of $V$ are represented by complex-valued functions in one variable, with adjoints given by conjugation and inner products given by integration.
To account for possible toral boundaries of $M$, however, one must revert back to the hyperbolic structure.

Using the leading term in [\[qdl-hbarexpansion\]](#qdl-hbarexpansion){reference-type="eqref" reference="qdl-hbarexpansion"}, we can approximate it to leading order as $$H (M;\hbar, u) \; \underset{\hbar \to 0}{\sim} \; \int\,e^{\frac{1}{\hbar} V(p_1, \ldots, p_{N-1}, u)}\; dp_1 \ldots dp_{N-1}\,, \label{Hik_V_limit}$$ with the "potential" $$V({\bf p},u) \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^N \epsilon_i \text{Li}_2(-\exp(g_i({\bf p},2u) + i\pi \epsilon_i))+\frac{1}{2} f({\bf p},2u,\hbar=0)\,. \label{Hik_gen_V}$$ As explained below [\[qdl-hbarexpansion\]](#qdl-hbarexpansion){reference-type="eqref" reference="qdl-hbarexpansion"}, the branches of $\text{Li}_2$ must be chosen appropriately to coincide with the half-lines of poles and zeroes of the quantum dilogarithms in [\[gen_Hik_integral\]](#gen_Hik_integral){reference-type="eqref" reference="gen_Hik_integral"}.
Again, the cuts of the logarithm must match the singularities of the quantum dilogarithm.

Thus, some irreducible component of $\overline{\phi(\cal R)}$, coming from an irreducible component of $\cal R$, must coincide with the entire irreducible component of ${\cal L}$ containing the geometric branch.

Moreover, if such a solution ${\bf x}^{(\alpha)}$ (corresponding to branch $\alpha$) can be lifted to a real critical point ${\bf p}^{(\alpha)} (u)$ of $V$, then one must have relations [\[lValpha\]](#lValpha){reference-type="eqref" reference="lValpha"} and [\[SValpha\]](#SValpha){reference-type="eqref" reference="SValpha"}.
To understand this correction factor, we must look at the higher-order terms in the expansion of $Z^{(\alpha)}(M;\hbar,u)$.

The former depends on the total number of tetrahedra, $N$, in the triangulation of $M$ and therefore must be cancelled (at least partially) since the total integral [\[statesumdef\]](#statesumdef){reference-type="eqref" reference="statesumdef"} is a topological invariant and cannot depend on $N$.
Which 3-manifolds shall we choose for our examples?
In particular, we shall verify the arithmeticity conjecture formulated in Section [\[sec:loops\]](#sec:loops){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:loops"}.

According to the Generalized Volume Conjecture [@gukov-2003], the invariant ${\cal J}(K;N)$ should have the asymptotics[^1] $$\label{JKn} {\cal J}(K;N) \;\sim\; \frac{ Z^{\text{(geom)}}(M;\,i\pi/N)} {Z({\bf S}^1 \times {\bf D}^2;\,i\pi/N)}\;\sim\;N^{3/2}\, \exp\left( \sum_{n=0}^\infty s_n \biggl(\frac{2\pi i}N\biggr)^{n-1} \right)$$ as $N\to\infty$, where $$\begin{aligned} S_n^{(\rm geom)}(0) & = s_n \cdot 2^{n-1} \qquad(n \ne 1) \label{Ss} \\ S_1^{(\rm geom)}(0) & = s_1 + \frac{1}{2} \log 2 \qquad(n=1) \nonumber \end{aligned}$$ are the perturbative $SL(2,{\mathbb{C}})$ invariants of $M = {\bf S}^3 \smallsetminus K$.

candidates.statement: As explained in Section [\[sec:ideal\]](#sec:ideal){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:ideal"}, the shape parameters $z$ and $w$ must obey consistency relations, which in the case of the figure-eight knot reduce to a single algebraic relation (see *e.g.* Chapter 4 of [@thurston-1980] and Section 15 of [@neumann-2004]): $$(z-1)(w-1)=z^2w^2 \,. \label{figeightgluing}$$ The shape parameters $z$ and $w$ are related to the $SL(2,{\mathbb{C}})$ holonomy eigenvalue, $l$, along the longitude[^1] of the knot in the following way $$\frac{z^2}{z-1} = -l\,, \qquad \frac{w^2}{w-1} = - l^{-1}\,, \label{lholviashape}$$ which automatically solves the consistency condition [\[figeightgluing\]](#figeightgluing){reference-type="eqref" reference="figeightgluing"}.

candidates.statement: From the relation [\[lholviashape\]](#lholviashape){reference-type="eqref" reference="lholviashape"} we find that the point $(l,m)=(-1,1)$ corresponding to the complete hyperbolic structure on $M$ is characterized by the values of $z$ and $w$ which solve the equation $$z^2 - z + 1 = 0\,.$$ In order to obtain tetrahedra of positive (signed) volume, we must choose $z$ to be the root of this equation with a positive imaginary part, and $w$ its inverse: $$z = \frac{1 + i \sqrt{3}}{2}\,,\qquad w= \frac{1 - i \sqrt{3}}{2}\,.$$ These value correspond to regular ideal tetrahedra, and maximize (respectively, minimize) the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm function $D(z)$.

candidates.statement: [^1]: Note that [@garoufalidis-2004; @garoufalidis-2006] look at asymptotics of the colored Jones polynomial normalized by its value at the unknot, while the $SL(2,{\mathbb{C}})$ Chern-Simons partition function should agree with the unnormalized colored Jones polynomial.
Hence, we must divide the expressions for $a_j$ there by $(m^2 q^{j/2} - q^{-j/2})$ to account for the difference, introducing a few factors of $q^{1/2}$ in our formulas.

$\overline{\hspace{2in}}$\ According to [\[sonetorsion\]](#sonetorsion){reference-type="eqref" reference="sonetorsion"}, the coefficient $S_1^{({\rm geom})} (u)$ in the perturbative Chern-Simons partition function should be related to the Reidemeister-Ray-Singer torsion of $M$ twisted by ${\cal A}^{({\rm geom})}$, which has been independently computed.

In the language of Section [\[sec:symmetries\]](#sec:symmetries){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:symmetries"}, the abelian branch must be its own "signed pair," guaranteeing that all even $S_{2k}^{(\rm abel)}(u)$ vanish.
[^2]: This expression assumes that $\Upsilon_{j,k}=0$ when $k$ is even, a fact that shall be explained momentarily.
Although a similar set of gluing rules should exist in a theory with complex gauge group GC, they are expected to be more involved than in the compact case.
As we shall see, in general, the information about the gauge group GC and the 3-manifold M is mixed within S(ρ) n (M) in a non-trivial way.

For example, when M is a knot complement, one can combine approaches 2 and 3 to learn that the operators bAi in (1.12) should also annihilate the polynomial invariants PG,R(K; q) computed by Chern-Simons gauge theory with compact gauge group G, bAi PG,R(K; q) = 0 .
